findings.evidence: The proof at lines 359-363 obtains `g : G`, coerces it into the normalizer only via `simp [Subgroup.normalizer_eq_top]`, and then uses `normalizerQuotientOrbitRelQuotient_smul_mk`; the nearby API already defines the descended action for arbitrary `H` at lines 303 and 321.
findings.fix: Add the general theorem with signature like `[MulAction.IsPretransitive (_root_.Subgroup.normalizer (H : Set G)) X] : letI := normalizerQuotientOrbitRelQuotientMulAction (X := X) H; MulAction.IsPretransitive (Subgroup.normalizerQuotient H) (MulAction.orbitRel.Quotient H X)`, then make the normal theorem a corollary using `Subgroup.normalizer_eq_top`.
findings.issue: `normalizerQuotientOrbitRelQuotientIsPretransitiveOfNormal` assumes `[MulAction.IsPretransitive G X]` and `[H.Normal]`, but the argument only needs representatives from `Subgroup.normalizer (H : Set G)` carrying `x` to `y`.

findings.evidence: Line 190 is just the generic theorem specialized to `X := p ⁻¹' {b}`; the local action instance exists for arbitrary `H` at line 151, so the normality restriction is inherited from the under-general generic theorem rather than needed by this wrapper.
findings.fix: Add `normalizerQuotientSubgroupFiberOrbitIsPretransitive` assuming `[MulAction.IsPretransitive (_root_.Subgroup.normalizer (H : Set (Deck p))) (p ⁻¹' {b})]`, and derive the existing normal and `of_isRegular` variants from it.
findings.issue: The fibre theorem repeats the same over-specialization to normal `H` instead of exposing the natural normalizer-action transitivity assumption for arbitrary subgroups.

summary: The new transitivity API is specialized to normal subgroups even though the proof only needs transitivity of the normalizer action itself. Prove the normalizer-level theorem first and derive the normal and regular-cover corollaries from it.
